triggers: a kernel on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942) risks the '5. aiter CK-tile bias is 2D (S,S) — cannot represent per-batch masks' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942): 5. aiter CK-tile bias is 2D (S,S) — cannot represent per-batch masks

problem.statement: Pitfalls: FlyDSL Flash Attention Backward — Arbitrary Mask Integration on MI308X -- 5. aiter CK-tile bias is 2D (S,S) — cannot represent per-batch masks

payload.attempted: When benchmarking against aiter's `mha_bwd` with bias, you might expect to pass the full (B, 1, S, S) mask as bias.
payload.lesson: aiter CK-tile backward with bias only handles the case where all sequences share the same mask pattern. For per-batch arbitrary masks (common in training with variable-length packed sequences), aiter cannot be used. This is a fundamental capability gap — not just a performance difference. FlyDSL's approach (bit-packed per-batch mask with precomputed loop bounds) supports the general case.

established_fact.mechanism: aiter's CK-tile backward kernel hardcodes `batch_stride_bias = 0` and `nhead_stride_bias = 0` — the same 2D (S, S) bias is broadcast identically across all batches and heads. This is a kernel-level design limitation of CK's fused backward implementation.

payload.observed: RuntimeError from CK kernel: `bias.sizes() == {seqlen_q, seqlen_k}` assertion fails. Bias must be exactly 2D.
payload.root_cause: aiter's CK-tile backward kernel hardcodes `batch_stride_bias = 0` and `nhead_stride_bias = 0` — the same 2D (S, S) bias is broadcast identically across all batches and heads. This is a kernel-level design limitation of CK's fused backward implementation.
